- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: _render_ticked at the `- [x]` substitution; tick() body construction for the appended comment (calls `_render_ticked(body, stable_sha, source_match.group(1))`). | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]

- scripts/operator_step_issue.py: tick() — `for key in sorted(latest)` loop with `_render_ticked` and the unconditional `_gh(...)` comment write per ticked key. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `tick` invocations can both append ticked comments for the same key from the same snapshot.
  WHY: The later write becomes authoritative, can mask a newer upsert, and leaves the earlier write as dead weight.
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py
  Location: tick() — `if any(DONE_RE.match(line) for line in lines): outcome = "already_done"` plus the analogous `DONE_RE` scan inside `_render_ticked` consumers (none currently).
  Issue: The DONE_RE scan matches against `lines = [line.strip() for line in body.split("\n")]`, i.e. every line of the body — including step instruction lines. The companion `test_operator_step_model_text_cannot_forge_tick_markers` only exercises source-field injection; if the verifier model emits a step whose `title` or `instructions` happens to contain `<!-- ai:operator-step:done stable=<40hex> -->`, that line will be picked up by `DONE_RE` and the entry will be reported as `already_done` on every subsequent tick run. `_clean` does not strip HTML-comment-shaped strings, so the marker survives verbatim.
  Suggested minimal fix: scan only the trailing marker area (e.g., `if any(DONE_RE.match(line) for line in lines[-3:])`), since `_render_ticked` always appends the done marker at the end of the ticked body.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
- scripts/operator_step_issue.py
  Location: tick() — `number = int(candidates[0]["number"])` immediately after `find_issues(issues)`.
  Issue: The pick trusts `candidates[0]["number"]` without a defensive `isinstance(candidates[0], dict)` check and without validating that `"number"` exists and is an integer. A malformed listing payload that passes the JSON parse but returns a non-dict (or a dict with a non-numeric `"number"`) raises `TypeError` instead of the documented `ApiError`, leaving the operator with a stack trace and no "list returned an unexpected shape" signal.
  Suggested minimal fix: validate `isinstance(candidates[0], dict)` and `isinstance(candidates[0].get("number"), int)` before the cast; otherwise raise `ApiError(f"unexpected issue list shape: {type(issues).__name__}")`.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
